note: Consider (consider.co, the firm's 2020 enterprise tile link) runs job boards and talent networks for venture firms; its site was live on 2026-09-30. No round naming Kleiner Perkins was found, and no source placed its headquarters.
Cooliris was acquired by Yahoo on 2014-11-21 (Wikipedia, which lists Kleiner Perkins among its backers). The archived page ties it to the iFund; the round the firm first entered is not on record.
CoroNet (network management software) was acquired by Compuware per the firm's own exit field; the firm's since-year is 1994 and no round is named. No source placed its headquarters.
CoSine Communications (IPO 2000) wound down its operations in the mid-2000s and remained a shell; defunct and Redwood City as in TCV's row. No round naming Kleiner Perkins is on record.

CreditEase (Tina Ju, KPCB China) is a Beijing lending and wealth platform whose own site names its Beijing entity; the member is CreditEase itself, not its listed subsidiary Yirendai (decisions.md R5). No priced round with a published valuation was found, so below_1b under Rule A; the round KPCB China entered is not on record.

Crittercism renamed itself Apteligent and was acquired by VMware (announced 2017-05-15, Wikipedia). The archived page ties it to the iFund (Ellen Pao); the round the firm first entered is not on record here.
Crystal Semiconductor (Austin) was acquired by Cirrus Logic in a stock swap completed in late October 1991 (Wikipedia). The firm's since-year is 1986; no round is named.

Wikipedia: Technology Partners and Kleiner Perkins provided Crystal Dynamics with seed capital (1992, the firm's since-year). King World then bought 10% for $7.5M in September 1993, an unnamed later priced round above the $5M step for an entry to 2014, so the seed graduated. Acquired by Eidos in 1998; based in San Carlos per Wikipedia.

CSG Systems (IPO 1996) was acquired by NEC, announced October 2025 and completed May 2026 (Wikipedia). The firm's since-year 1994 is the year CSG Holdings bought the business from First Data; the record does not name the firm's round, so the stage is undetermined.

funding_rounds.round: acquisition of Cable Services Group by CSG Holdings (Morgan Stanley, Trident)

note: Kleiner Perkins co-led CuspAI's $450M Series B at $2.6B with NEA (Pulse 2.0, 2026-07-20; the firm's own post of the same day says it co-led the Series B); the site's since-year is 2026, so the B is the entry. Cambridge, UK. Momentum check 2026-09-30: this round is the $1B+ priced round.
CyOptics (InP optical chips, Breinigsville PA) was acquired by Avago Technologies in 2013. Vinod Khosla is the partner on the archived page, a pre-2004 Kleiner Perkins seat; no round is named.

Status disputed: Infineon completed its acquisition of Cypress on 2020-04-17 (Wikipedia), so acquired, not defunct. Cypress was formed in 1982 with backing from Sevin Rosen, Kleiner Perkins, Mayfield and Sequoia; the round is not named.

Danoo (place-based digital media screens) appears on the firm's 2008-09 list only and left it by 2010; a Google News search for the name returned nothing about the company, so its fate and city are not established.

Dash Navigation was acquired by Research In Motion (announced June 2009). Mountain View per Wikipedia and the firm's own 2008-10 listing; Sequoia's row reads Sunnyvale from model knowledge. The firm's entry round (Matt Murphy) is not on record.
Datou, a Beijing mobile multimedia software company on the KPCB China list (Beijing per the firm's own 2009-10 China listing); its later fate is not established and no round is named.

Deosen, a xanthan gum manufacturer on the KPCB China list, located only as 'Shandong, China' (a province) by the firm's 2009-10 listing; the city and its current state are not established, and no round is named.

Status disputed: the firm's own record gives Destineer (1992, networking for telecom carriers) as acquired by MCI WorldCom; the prefilled defunct matches the unrelated video game publisher of the same name. No source placed its headquarters and no round is named.

Devicescape (founded 2001 in San Francisco as Instant802 Networks, renamed 2005) was acquired by Pareteum on 2019-05-08 (Wikipedia). The two base rows devicescape-formerly-instant-802-networks-inc and devicescape-software-inc are one company. The firm's round (Doug Mackenzie) is not on record.

Devicescape (founded 2001 in San Francisco as Instant802 Networks, renamed 2005) was acquired by Pareteum on 2019-05-08 (Wikipedia). The two base rows devicescape-formerly-instant-802-networks-inc and devicescape-software-inc are one company. The firm's round (Doug Mackenzie) is not on record.

DHgate, a Beijing cross-border B2B marketplace (Wikipedia), held by KPCB China (Tina Ju, Xin Tang). No priced round with a published valuation was found, so below_1b under Rule A; KPCB China's round is not on record.
Diamond Lane Communications (DSL equipment, Petaluma) was acquired by Nokia per the firm's own exit field; since-year 1995, no round named.
Dichanphone (pre-installed real estate phone apps) appears on the firm's 2012-17 pages under Team China (Xin Tang); no source gives its city, fate or round.
Digital Chocolate (Trip Hawkins, 2003, San Mateo) sold its games to RockYou and shut its site (Wikipedia); the firm's round (Russell Siegelman) is not on record.

Kleiner Perkins joined Discovery Loop's initial round, led by Radical Ventures and Khosla Ventures (Business Insider via Investing.com, 2026-09-11); reports call it a seed, and the firm lists it Early 2026. Momentum check 2026-09-30: the $10B figure was reported as talks and a new round seeks about $50B, neither a closed priced round, so below_1b with needs_web_value. Censored: entered 2026.
DJZ (electronic dance music media, Mike Abbott, 2014); status unknown as in GV's row, city not established, no round naming Kleiner Perkins found.

DMX Technologies Group, an SGX Main Board company headquartered in Hong Kong, became a consolidated KDDI subsidiary when KDDI subscribed new shares for 52.56% (KDDI release 2009-09-10). The KPCB China position was likely taken after the SGX listing (a T3 question raised in the report); no round is named.

Seed investors including Kleiner Perkins put in $1M in March 2012 and the same group with Venrock the $9.8M Series A in October 2012 (Wikipedia), so the seed graduated. Acquired by Unilever in 2016. City Durham: the company opened its new headquarters there in September 2025 (Wikipedia), fresher than the siblings' Los Angeles.

Doodle Mobile, a Chinese mobile game developer on the firm's 2013-17 pages under Teams China and Digital (Wei Zhou, Matt Murphy); Beijing from model knowledge. Its fate and the round are not established.

eASIC (founded 1999, Santa Clara) was acquired by Intel in 2018 (Wikipedia). Its 2014 draft S-1 lists KPCB Holdings among holders exchanging into Series A-2 stock in a recapitalisation; the firm's first round (Vinod Khosla's KP-era seat) is not named.
Echelon (founded 1988, IPO 1998) was acquired by Adesto Technologies on 2018-09-14 and was based in Santa Clara (Wikipedia). The firm's round is not on record.
EdeniQ (biofuel process technology, Visalia CA; John Denniston) is on the firm's 2013-18 pages; its current state is not established and no round is named.

effx (microservices catalog, 2018-2021) announced on its own site that 'effx is joining the team at Figma' (read 2026-09-30), and the firm lists it among alumni; Kleiner Perkins' Bucky Moore was an early investor and EIR, but the round is not named.
Elance merged with oDesk in 2013 to form Elance-oDesk, now Upwork (Wikipedia); acquired and Mountain View as in NEA's row. The firm's round is not on record.

elcomax (fuel cell combined heat and power, partners Brook Porter and Jan van Dokkum, 2013-18 pages); its domain elcomax.de no longer resolves and its fate and city are not established; no round named.
Element Analytics (industrial data operations) is on the firm's 2017-18 pages with no detail; its round, current state and city are not established here.

Emdeon Corporation is the 2005 name of Healtheon/WebMD (the firm's 1996 Healtheon investment), renamed HLTH in 2007 and merged into WebMD Health Corp in 2009, itself bought by Internet Brands in 2017; the same company as the base rows healtheon and webmd-corp-new.
ENDFORCE, an Ohio network access control company, was acquired by Sophos in 2007 (Wikipedia, Sophos article); the firm's tile links to sophos.com. No round named.
eNet, a Beijing IT-industry portal on the firm's 2009-10 China listing; status unknown as in Redpoint's row, no round named.

The firm's own post says it led Engram's Series A as the company emerged with $98M across seed and Series A (company release, San Francisco, 2026-06-23); Sequoia's row holds the earlier seed. Momentum check 2026-09-30: Calcalist headlines the $98M at a $600M valuation and Google News shows no later round, so below_1b.

note: Enlighted (smart building sensors and controls, Sunnyvale; Trae Vassallo) was acquired by Siemens in 2022; the firm's round is not on record.

Eo, Inc., 52 percent owned by AT&T, shut down operations on 1994-07-29 (Wikipedia, EO Personal Communicator); the site's 'acquired by AT&T' reflects the 1993 majority stake, but the business ended, so defunct. Since-year 1991, no round named.
eRecyclingCorps (device trade-in and resale, Green Growth Fund) renamed itself HYLA Mobile and was acquired by Assurant in 2020 (model knowledge). The Green Growth Fund round is not cited here.
Erly (a social collections app, sFund, Chi-Hua Chien) shows as Acquired on the firm's 2013-14 pages; the acquirer, city and the round are not established.
eSionic (molecular systems for energy storage, Mark Allen) is on the firm's 2012-14 pages only; its fate, city and round are not established.
